project.topic: What if the Moon orbited at half its current distance?
project.title: What If the Moon Were Twice as Close?
project.audience: Curious global general audiences age 13+, no astronomy background
project.core_question: How would a closer Moon reshape our nights, tides, ecosystems, and coastal life?
project.viewer_takeaway: A visually modest doubling of the Moon’s angular width can have much bigger tidal implications, without implying a universal eightfold rise in water level.

scientific_model.baseline_reality: Mean Earth–Moon center distance is about 384,400 km and the sidereal orbital period is about 27.32 days. A full Moon spans roughly half a degree in the sky; lunar and solar forcing jointly influence tides.
scientific_model.counterfactual_change: Instantaneously move the Moon onto a near-circular orbit at 192,200 km center-to-center while preserving its mass, radius, lunar surface appearance, and Earth’s mean orbital and spin properties at the start.
assumptions: An external hypothetical intervention supplies the orbital energy and angular-momentum change needed to establish a stable near-circular orbit at 192,200 km; it is not simply released from rest at half distance.
Use simplified Kepler scaling for the new lunar period; do not predict the long-term coupled Earth–Moon evolution within this 50-second short.
Retain present Earth geography and ocean basins initially; coastline flooding and habitat responses vary regionally and over time.
Use correct relative moon angular widths in sky shots; label purely explanatory orbital and tide diagrams as schematics.
causal_chain: Half the distance with unchanged diameter makes the Moon’s angular diameter roughly twice as large.
Lunar tide-generating differential gravity scales approximately with distance inverse-cubed, yielding 2^3 = 8 times its present lunar contribution.
Ocean tidal heights depend on coast shape, bathymetry, basin resonance, friction, and solar forcing, so no global eightfold tide height follows.
Shorter orbital radius reduces lunar sidereal period by 2^(3/2): from roughly 27.3 days to roughly 9.7 days.
Altered tides and timing could create serious coastal and intertidal ecological pressures, with strongly location-dependent outcomes.
uncertainties: Exact tidal range at any coastline requires hydrodynamic simulation and cannot be inferred by multiplying present tide height by eight.
Human vulnerability depends on geography, adaptation and time horizon; flooding is illustrative, not universally guaranteed.
A longer-term Earth–Moon dynamic response and tidal heating are intentionally outside the scope of this immediate comparison.

claims.statement: Baseline Moon distance ≈384,400 km and orbital period ≈27.3 days.
claims.reasoning: NASA Moon orbital parameters and measurements.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Use approximate labels and specify center-to-center orbit scale.

claims.statement: At half the distance, apparent lunar angular diameter is approximately twice today’s size.
claims.reasoning: For fixed diameter at large distance, angular diameter is approximately proportional to 1/d.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Do not show a Moon occupying most of the entire sky; telephoto close-ups are camera effects.

claims.statement: The Moon’s tide-generating force contribution becomes approximately eight times its baseline.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Never claim real-world tide HEIGHTS are all eight times larger.

claims.statement: Local coastal tidal conditions could be dramatically altered.
claims.reasoning: Greater differential lunar forcing changes tidal response; local morphology and dynamics determine actual water levels.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Say could, not would; scene is an illustrative vulnerable bay, not a universal simulation.

claims.statement: Intertidal habitats could shift under a stronger, altered tidal regime.
claims.reasoning: Changes in water exposure, inundation, flow and timing alter coastal ecological niches.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Avoid assuming every species vanishes; show stress and adjustment rather than total collapse.

claims.statement: For an approximately circular half-radius orbit, Moon’s sidereal period becomes about 9.7 days instead of 27.3.
claims.presentation_guardrail: Nine-to-ten days is the orbit relative to distant stars, not the duration of an Earth day.

creative_direction.logline: A strangely bigger Moon glides over a sleeping coastal city; its beauty hides a much stronger gravitational tidal rhythm that changes shores and the speed of our lunar month.
creative_direction.visual_identity: Photoreal celestial photography meets human-scale eco-documentary; detailed crater relief, atmospheric scattering, wet shoreline speculars, restrained cinematic depth of field. No fantasy apocalypse.
creative_direction.lighting: Physically motivated cold moonlight against warm coastal practical lights; nuanced volumetric haze and water reflections.
creative_direction.camera_language: Start with compressed telephoto city framing; reveal accurate side-by-side lunar angular size; cut to precise diagram; descend to human-eye coastal tide; macro ecology; return to serene sky.
creative_direction.motion_language: Elegant slow orbit/dolly; one decisive cause-and-effect transition per beat; purposeful water movement; no frantic zooms.
creative_direction.world_scale_policy: Use Earth radius 1 scene unit and Moon radius 0.273 units in planetary and accurate angular-size comparisons, Moon orbital radii 60.34 and 30.17 Earth radii. For detailed terrestrial shots use meters; diagrammatic orbital spacing may be changed only with an on-screen SCHEMATIC label.
creative_direction.opening_hook: A real-sized Moon visibly shifts to a larger angular diameter in the telephoto skyline while the question lands instantly.
creative_direction.ending_payoff: The same city/moon composition returns serene but now a subtle altered tide mark tells the story, then matches the opening moon position for seamless loop.
creative_direction.loop_connection: Last moon glide and camera tilt line up with the first shot, letting first-line question continue the sense of wonder.
creative_direction.asset_policy: Build procedural starfields, ocean, weather, harbor silhouettes, vegetation and rock pools in Three.js; optionally use freely licensed NASA lunar texture with attribution record, otherwise procedural lunar albedo/normal maps. No paid assets or unverified downloads.

audio.voice_style: Calm, peaceful, warm adult male; intimate documentary voice; natural breathing; wonder without shouting
audio.music_direction: Very subtle original warm synth pads, distant bowed-glass undertones, low-end pulse growing during tidal mechanism, resolve to single suspended note at end; almost silent under voice.
audio.sfx_direction: Soft nocturnal sea, wind, barely perceptible tidal sub-bass swell, isolated gentle swoosh; never a loud cinematic impact.

captions.style: Premium documentary subtitles: ivory semibold, thin charcoal outline and shadow, restrained sea-glass word highlight, soft 100ms ease; phrase-by-phrase lower-middle overlay.
captions.active_word_treatment: One key word at a time receives soft sea-glass color and tiny 1.04x scale without popping or moving baselines.
captions.highlights_policy: Exact narration only; selectively accent important mechanisms and numbers; never add unsupported factual captions.

distribution.primary_search_intent: What happens to Earth, the oceans and humans if the Moon moves twice as close?
core_keywords: what if the moon was closer
distribution.distinctive_angle: The Moon only doubles in apparent width, while lunar tide-generating forcing increases roughly eightfold under fixed-mass distance assumptions.
distribution.seo_integrity_note: Never translate eightfold lunar tidal forcing into eightfold local water heights; retain scientific uncertainty in titles and descriptions.
